starter.overnight_oats.title: Overnight oats
steps: Stir the oats, milk, yogurt and chia seeds together in a jar or bowl.
Cover and chill overnight, or for at least four hours.
Slice the banana on top and drizzle with honey to serve.
starter.overnight_oats.notes: Leave out the honey for children under one. Keeps in the fridge for two days, so make a double batch.

starter.lentil_tomato_soup.title: Lentil and tomato soup
steps: Warm the oil in a large pan and cook the onion and carrot gently for about 8 minutes.
Add the garlic and cumin and cook for a minute more.
Add the lentils, tomatoes and stock, then simmer for 25 minutes, until the lentils are soft.
Blend if you like it smooth, and season with salt to taste.
starter.lentil_tomato_soup.notes: Cool, then freeze in single portions for up to three months.

starter.chicken_traybake.title: One-tray chicken and sweet potato
steps: Heat the oven to {oven:200}.
Toss the chicken, sweet potato and onion with the oil, paprika, salt and pepper on a large baking sheet.
Roast for 25 minutes, add the broccoli, then roast for 15 minutes more, until the chicken reaches {temp:74} in the thickest part.
starter.chicken_traybake.notes: Leftovers keep in the fridge for three days and make a quick lunch.

starter.banana_pancakes.title: Banana pancakes
steps: Mash the banana well, then whisk in the eggs, flour and baking powder.
Melt a little butter in a frying pan over medium heat.
Cook small spoonfuls for about 2 minutes on each side, until golden and cooked through.
Let them cool before serving to little ones. Babies can hold a whole small pancake or a strip.

starter.cheesy_pasta_peas.title: Cheesy pasta with peas
steps: Cook the pasta in a large pan of boiling water, adding the peas for the last 3 minutes.
Drain, then stir in the butter, milk and cheese over low heat until creamy.
For toddlers, squash the peas a little with a fork.

starter.spinach_egg_muffins.title: Spinach and cheese egg muffins
steps: Heat the oven to {oven:180} and brush the holes of a 12-hole muffin tin with oil.
Divide the spinach, bell pepper, scallions and cheese between the holes.
Whisk the eggs with the milk and a little black pepper, then pour over the vegetables.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until puffed and set in the middle and a knife pushed in comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 5 minutes before lifting them out.
starter.spinach_egg_muffins.notes: Freeze cooled muffins in a freezer bag for up to two months. Reheat from frozen in the microwave for about a minute, until hot all the way through.

starter.peanut_butter_banana_toast.title: Peanut butter and banana toast
steps: Toast the bread.
Spread the peanut butter over the toast while it is still warm.
Slice the banana over the top and dust with cinnamon.
starter.peanut_butter_banana_toast.notes: For a baby or toddler, spread the peanut butter thinly and cut the toast into fingers.

starter.breakfast_burritos.title: Freezer breakfast burritos
steps: Whisk the eggs with the milk.
Warm the oil in a large frying pan over medium-low heat. Add the eggs and stir slowly until they are fully set, with no runny egg left, then take the pan off the heat.
Warm the tortillas briefly so they fold without cracking.
Spoon beans, egg, cheese, scallions and a little salsa down the middle of each tortilla. Fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
Eat straight away, or cool completely, wrap each one in foil and freeze.
starter.breakfast_burritos.notes: Freeze for up to two months. To reheat, unwrap, wrap in a damp paper towel and microwave for 2 to 3 minutes, turning halfway, until steaming hot in the middle.

starter.banana_oat_muffins.title: Banana and blueberry oat muffins
steps: Heat the oven to {oven:180} and line a 12-hole muffin tin with muffin liners, or grease it well.
Mash the bananas until smooth, then whisk in the eggs, milk and oil.
Stir in the oats, flour, baking powder and cinnamon until just combined, then fold in the blueberries.
Fill the holes about three-quarters full and bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until risen and a skewer pushed into the middle comes out clean.
Cool on a rack. For babies, break into strips or pieces they can hold.
starter.banana_oat_muffins.notes: No added sugar: the bananas sweeten them. Freeze for up to three months and thaw at room temperature.

starter.hummus_veggie_wraps.title: Hummus and crunchy vegetable wraps
steps: Spread the hummus over each tortilla, leaving a border.
Scatter over the spinach, carrot, cucumber and feta, and squeeze over a little lemon juice.
Roll up tightly, then cut in half on an angle.
starter.hummus_veggie_wraps.notes: Wrapped tightly, these keep in the fridge until the next day.

starter.tuna_white_bean_salad.title: Tuna and white bean salad
steps: Whisk the lemon juice and oil with a little salt and pepper in a bowl.
Add the beans, tomatoes and onion and toss to coat.
Flake in the tuna, scatter with parsley and fold through gently.
starter.tuna_white_bean_salad.notes: Good with crusty bread or over salad leaves. Keeps in the fridge for a day.

starter.chickpea_salad_sandwich.title: Smashed chickpea sandwiches
steps: Mash the chickpeas roughly with a fork, leaving some texture.
Stir in the mayonnaise, mustard, lemon juice, celery and chives, and add black pepper to taste.
Spread between slices of bread.
starter.chickpea_salad_sandwich.notes: The filling keeps in the fridge for up to three days.

starter.veggie_fried_rice.title: Vegetable fried rice
steps: Heat half the oil in a large frying pan or wok over high heat. Add the eggs and stir until set, then tip them onto a plate.
Add the rest of the oil, then the garlic and the white parts of the scallions, and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the frozen vegetables and stir-fry for 3 minutes, until hot.
Break up the rice, add it to the pan and stir-fry for 4 to 5 minutes, until steaming hot all the way through.
Stir in the soy sauce, sesame oil, egg and scallion greens.
starter.veggie_fried_rice.notes: Cool cooked rice quickly and keep it in the fridge for no more than a day before frying. Reheat rice only once.

lineNotes.0: cooked a day ahead and chilled

starter.black_bean_quesadillas.title: Black bean and cheese quesadillas
steps: Mash half the beans with the cumin, then stir in the rest of the beans and the corn.
Spread the bean mix over half of each tortilla, scatter with cheese and fold over.
Cook in a lightly oiled frying pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes on each side, until crisp and the cheese has melted.
Cut into wedges and serve with salsa and sour cream.

starter.minestrone.title: Big-batch minestrone
steps: Warm the oil in a large pot and cook the onion, carrot and celery gently for 10 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic, zucchini and Italian seasoning and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, beans and stock, bring to a boil, then simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the pasta and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until tender, stirring now and then. Stir in the spinach until it wilts.
Season with salt and pepper and serve with Parmesan.
starter.minestrone.notes: Cool and freeze without the Parmesan for up to three months. The pasta softens when reheated, which most children don't mind.

starter.beef_bolognese.title: Freezer-friendly bolognese
steps: Warm the oil in a large heavy pan and cook the onion, carrot and celery over medium heat for 10 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic and cook for a minute, then add the beef. Break it up and cook until browned all over with no pink left, and it reaches {temp:71}.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, then add the tomatoes, stock, oregano and bay leaves.
Simmer gently, partly covered, for 45 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick.
Take out the bay leaves, season with salt and pepper, and serve over spaghetti.
starter.beef_bolognese.notes: Freeze cooled sauce in portions for up to three months. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat until piping hot.

starter.turkey_meatballs.title: Baked turkey and zucchini meatballs
steps: Heat the oven to {oven:200} and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Mix the turkey, breadcrumbs, egg, Parmesan, zucchini, garlic and oregano with your hands until just combined.
Roll into balls about the size of a ping-pong ball, set them on the baking sheet and brush with the oil.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until browned, with no pink in the middle, and they reach {temp:74}.
Meanwhile, simmer the tomatoes with the basil for 10 minutes. Add the meatballs and turn them in the sauce.
For toddlers, cut the meatballs into quarters.
starter.turkey_meatballs.notes: Freeze baked meatballs on a tray, then bag them, for up to three months. Reheat in the sauce until piping hot.

starter.chicken_coconut_curry.title: Mild chicken and coconut curry
steps: Warm the oil in a large pan and cook the onion over medium heat for 8 minutes, until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, ginger and curry powder and stir for a minute, until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir to coat it in the spices, then add the tomatoes and coconut milk.
Simmer, partly covered, for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the chicken is tender and reaches {temp:74}.
Stir in the spinach until it wilts, season with salt, and serve with rice and cilantro.
starter.chicken_coconut_curry.notes: Mild enough for most children. Freeze for up to three months, thaw in the fridge overnight and reheat until piping hot.

starter.beef_bean_chili.title: Beef and bean chili
steps: Warm the oil in a large pan and cook the onion and bell pepper over medium heat for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic and beef and cook, breaking the meat up, until browned with no pink left and it reaches {temp:71}.
Stir in the chili powder, cumin, paprika and tomato paste and cook for a minute.
Add the tomatoes, beans and stock. Simmer, partly covered, for 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick.
Season with salt and serve with sour cream and cheese.
starter.beef_bean_chili.notes: Freeze for up to three months. For children, use less chili powder and add heat to adult bowls at the table.

starter.salmon_potato_traybake.title: Salmon, potato and green bean traybake
steps: Heat the oven to {oven:200}.
Toss the potatoes with half the oil on a large baking sheet and roast for 15 minutes.
Push the potatoes to the sides, add the green beans and salmon, drizzle with the rest of the oil and lay the lemon slices on the salmon.
Roast for 12 to 15 minutes more, until the salmon flakes easily and reaches {temp:63} in the thickest part.
Scatter with dill. For toddlers, flake the salmon and check carefully for bones.
starter.salmon_potato_traybake.notes: Made without salt so the whole family can share it. Adults can salt their own plates.

starter.slow_cooker_pulled_pork.title: Slow-cooker pulled pork
steps: Mix the paprika, cumin, sugar and salt, and rub it all over the pork.
Put the onions and garlic in the slow cooker and sit the pork on top. Whisk the vinegar and tomato paste with a splash of water and pour it around the pork.
Cover and cook on low for 8 hours, until the pork is very tender, pulls apart easily and has reached at least {temp:90}.
Lift out the pork and shred it with two forks. Skim the fat from the juices, then stir the barbecue sauce and enough of the juices into the meat to keep it moist.
Serve in the buns.
starter.slow_cooker_pulled_pork.notes: Freeze in portions with some of the juices for up to three months. Also good in wraps or over rice.

starter.chicken_noodle_soup.title: Chicken noodle soup
steps: Warm the oil in a large pot and cook the onion, carrot and celery gently for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic for a minute, then the stock, thyme and bay leaf, and bring to a boil.
Add the chicken breasts whole, lower the heat and simmer gently for 15 to 20 minutes, until the chicken reaches {temp:74} in the thickest part.
Lift out the chicken, shred it with two forks and return it to the pot.
Add the noodles and simmer for 5 minutes, until tender. Take out the bay leaf, season with salt and pepper and stir in the parsley.
starter.chicken_noodle_soup.notes: To freeze, leave out the noodles and cook fresh ones when you reheat, so they don't go soft. Keeps frozen for three months.

starter.red_lentil_dal.title: Creamy red lentil dal
steps: Warm the oil in a large pan and cook the onion gently for 8 minutes, until soft.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and spices for a minute.
Add the lentils, tomatoes, coconut milk and water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring often, until the lentils have broken down and the dal is thick.
Stir in the spinach until it wilts, then the lemon juice.
For babies, serve it thick on a preloaded spoon, or with strips of soft flatbread or toast to dip. Grown-ups can stir salt and chili into their own bowls.
starter.red_lentil_dal.notes: Made without salt or stock, so it suits babies from around six months. Freeze in small portions, such as in an ice cube tray, for up to three months.

starter.fish_tacos.title: Quick fish tacos with lime slaw
steps: Rub the fish with the paprika, cumin, a little salt and the oil.
Toss the cabbage with half the lime juice and a pinch of salt. Stir the rest of the lime juice into the sour cream.
Cook the fish in a hot frying pan for 3 to 4 minutes on each side, until it is opaque all the way through and flakes easily.
Warm the tortillas. Flake the fish into them and top with the slaw, avocado, lime sour cream and cilantro, with lime wedges to squeeze.

starter.pesto_chicken_pasta.title: Pesto chicken pasta
steps: Cook the pasta in a large pan of salted boiling water until just tender. Save a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.
Meanwhile, warm the oil in a large frying pan and cook the chicken over medium-high heat for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until golden with no pink inside and it reaches {temp:74}.
Add the tomatoes for 2 minutes, then the spinach until it wilts.
Toss in the pasta, pesto and a splash of the cooking water until glossy. Serve with Parmesan.
starter.pesto_chicken_pasta.notes: Most pesto contains nuts and cheese, so check the jar if anyone has an allergy.

starter.zucchini_feta_frittata.title: Zucchini and feta frittata
steps: Heat the broiler to high.
Warm the oil in an ovenproof frying pan over medium heat and cook the zucchini and onion for 8 minutes, until soft. Stir in the spinach until it wilts.
Whisk the eggs with the milk, mint and pepper and pour over the vegetables. Scatter with the feta.
Cook over low heat for 6 to 8 minutes, until the edges are set.
Slide the pan under the broiler for 2 to 3 minutes, until the top is set and golden. Cool a little, then cut into wedges.
starter.zucchini_feta_frittata.notes: Eat warm or cold. Wedges keep in the fridge for three days and make an easy one-handed lunch.

starter.ginger_pork_stir_fry.title: Ginger pork and broccoli stir-fry
steps: Toss the pork with the cornstarch and a third of the soy sauce.
Mix the rest of the soy sauce with the honey, garlic, ginger and a splash of water.
Heat half the oil in a wok or large frying pan over high heat. Stir-fry the pork for 3 to 4 minutes, until browned and it reaches {temp:63}, then tip it onto a plate.
Add the rest of the oil and stir-fry the broccoli and bell pepper for 4 minutes, adding a splash of water to help the broccoli steam.
Return the pork with the sauce and scallions and toss for a minute, until glossy. Serve with rice.

starter.cauliflower_mac_cheese.title: Cauliflower mac and cheese
steps: Cook the pasta in a large pan of boiling water, adding the cauliflower for the last 5 minutes, until both are tender. Drain.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a pan, stir in the flour and cook for a minute.
Whisk in the milk a little at a time and keep stirring over medium heat until the sauce is smooth and thick.
Take it off the heat and stir in most of the cheese, the mustard and the nutmeg, then fold in the pasta and cauliflower.
Eat straight away, or tip it into a baking dish, scatter with the rest of the cheese and brown under the broiler.
starter.cauliflower_mac_cheese.notes: Freeze in portions for up to two months. Reheat with a splash of milk until piping hot.

starter.beef_vegetable_stew.title: Oven beef and vegetable stew
steps: Heat the oven to {oven:160}.
Toss the beef in the flour with a little salt and pepper. Brown it in batches in the oil in a large Dutch oven, then set it aside.
Lower the heat, add the onion, carrot and celery and cook for 8 minutes, then stir in the garlic and tomato paste.
Return the beef, add the stock, thyme and bay leaves, and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook in the oven for 1 hour.
Add the potatoes and cook for 1 hour more, until the beef is falling apart and has reached at least {temp:71}. Take out the bay leaves.
starter.beef_vegetable_stew.notes: Or cook it on low in a slow cooker for 8 hours. Freeze in portions for up to three months.

starter.shepherds_pie.title: Shepherd's pie
steps: Warm the oil in a large pan and cook the onion and carrot for 8 minutes. Add the lamb and cook, breaking it up, until browned with no pink left and it reaches {temp:71}. Spoon off any excess fat.
Stir in the tomato paste and flour for a minute, then add the stock, Worcestershire sauce and thyme. Simmer for 20 minutes, until thick, then stir in the peas and season with salt and pepper.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes for 15 to 20 minutes, until tender. Drain and mash with the butter and milk, and season.
Heat the oven to {oven:200}. Spoon the lamb into a baking dish, top with the mash and rough up the surface with a fork.
Bake for 25 minutes, until golden and bubbling at the edges.
starter.shepherds_pie.notes: To freeze, cool the assembled pie, cover and freeze for up to three months. Thaw overnight in the fridge, then bake for 40 minutes, until piping hot in the middle.

starter.sweet_potato_wedges.title: Soft sweet potato wedges
steps: Heat the oven to {oven:200} and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Cut the sweet potatoes into wedges about the size of an adult finger, and toss them with the oil and paprika.
Spread them out on the baking sheet and roast for 25 to 30 minutes, turning halfway, until soft enough to squash easily between your finger and thumb.
Cool until just warm before serving. Babies can hold a whole wedge. Peel off the skin if it is tough.
starter.sweet_potato_wedges.notes: A good first finger food from around six months, and a side for the rest of the family.

starter.salmon_fishcakes.title: Salmon and pea fishcakes
steps: Boil the potatoes for 15 minutes, until tender, then drain well and mash.
Mix in the salmon, peas, lemon zest, dill and egg until combined. Shape into eight small patties.
Press the patties into the breadcrumbs to coat. Chill them for 15 minutes if you have time, so they hold together.
Fry in the oil over medium heat for 4 minutes on each side, until golden, firm and cooked through.
For babies, cut into fingers, and check again for small bones.
starter.salmon_fishcakes.notes: Freeze uncooked patties on a tray, then bag them, for up to three months. Cook from frozen for a few minutes longer on each side, until hot all the way through.

starter.broccoli_cheese_bites.title: Broccoli and cheese bites
steps: Heat the oven to {oven:200} and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Steam or boil the broccoli for 5 minutes, until tender. Drain well, cool a little and chop it finely.
Mix the broccoli with the eggs, cheese, breadcrumbs and scallion. Shape into small logs or patties, about the size of a baby's palm.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and firm.
Cool before serving.
starter.broccoli_cheese_bites.notes: Keep in the fridge for two days, or freeze for up to two months.

starter.apple_cinnamon_oatmeal.title: Apple and cinnamon oatmeal
steps: Put the oats, milk, apple and cinnamon in a pan over medium heat.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 5 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy. Add a splash more milk if it gets too thick.
Cool a little before serving. For babies, make it thick enough to stay on a preloaded spoon.
starter.apple_cinnamon_oatmeal.notes: The apple sweetens it, so there is no added sugar. Grown-ups can sweeten their own bowls.

starter.lamb_koftas.title: Lamb and zucchini koftas
steps: Heat the oven to {oven:200} and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Mix the lamb, zucchini, onion, garlic, spices and half the mint with your hands.
Shape into twelve finger-sized logs that a baby can hold, set them on the baking sheet and brush with the oil.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, turning once, until browned all over, with no pink in the middle, and they reach {temp:71}.
Stir the cucumber and the rest of the mint into the yogurt to dip. Serve with warm pita.
starter.lamb_koftas.notes: Freeze cooked koftas for up to three months and reheat until piping hot.

starter.hidden_veg_tomato_sauce.title: Hidden vegetable tomato sauce
steps: Warm the oil in a large pan and cook the onion, carrot, zucchini and bell pepper gently for 15 minutes, until very soft.
Add the garlic for a minute, then the tomatoes. Rinse each can with a splash of water and add that too.
Simmer for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, then stir in the basil.
Blend until smooth.
Use it on pasta, as a pizza topping or for dipping. For babies, stir it through soft pasta shapes they can pick up.
starter.hidden_veg_tomato_sauce.notes: Made without salt or sugar, for babies. Freeze in portions, or in an ice cube tray for small helpings, for up to three months.

starter.avocado_toast_fingers.title: Avocado toast fingers
steps: Toast the bread lightly, so it is firm enough to hold but not hard.
Mash the avocado with the lemon juice and spread it thickly over the toast.
Cut into fingers about as wide as two adult fingers, and trim off any very crisp crusts.
starter.avocado_toast_fingers.notes: A thick layer of avocado helps babies grip the toast. For older children and adults, top it with an egg cooked until the yolk is firm.

starter.banana_oat_cookies.title: Banana oat cookies
steps: Heat the oven to {oven:180} and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Mash the bananas well, then stir in the oats, peanut butter and cinnamon. Leave for 5 minutes so the oats soften.
Drop spoonfuls onto the baking sheet and flatten each one.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until golden at the edges and firm to the touch.
Let them cool on the baking sheet, where they firm up further.
starter.banana_oat_cookies.notes: No added sugar. Keep in an airtight box for three days.

starter.yogurt_berry_pops.title: Frozen yogurt and berry popsicles
steps: Blend the yogurt, berries and banana until smooth.
Pour into popsicle molds, add sticks and freeze for at least six hours, until solid.
To get them out, hold the molds under warm water for a few seconds.
starter.yogurt_berry_pops.notes: Keep for up to a month in the freezer. A cooling snack on hot days.

starter.corn_zucchini_fritters.title: Corn and zucchini fritters
steps: Whisk the eggs, milk, flour and baking powder into a thick batter.
Stir in the corn, zucchini, scallions and cheese.
Heat a little oil in a frying pan over medium heat. Drop in spoonfuls of batter and flatten them slightly.
Cook for 3 minutes on each side, until golden and cooked through in the middle. Keep them warm while you cook the rest, adding oil as needed.
starter.corn_zucchini_fritters.notes: Freeze cooled fritters with parchment paper between them for up to two months. Reheat in a hot oven until hot all the way through.

starter.sticky_chicken_drumsticks.title: Sticky soy and honey drumsticks
steps: Heat the oven to {oven:200} and line a roasting pan with foil.
Mix the soy sauce, honey, garlic and ginger, and toss the drumsticks in it.
Roast for 40 to 45 minutes, turning and basting twice, until sticky and dark and the meat reaches {temp:74} near the bone.
Scatter with the sesame seeds and scallions.
starter.sticky_chicken_drumsticks.notes: Roast a double batch: cold drumsticks keep in the fridge for three days and travel well. Not for babies under one, because of the honey.

starter.sausage_bean_casserole.title: Sausage and bean casserole
steps: Brown the sausages in the oil in a large pan over medium heat for 8 minutes, turning, then lift them out and cut each into three.
Cook the onion and bell pepper in the same pan for 8 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic and paprika for a minute.
Add the tomatoes, beans, stock, thyme and sausages. Simmer, partly covered, for 15 to 20 minutes, until thick and the sausages reach {temp:71}.
starter.sausage_bean_casserole.notes: Serve with mashed potato or crusty bread. Freeze for up to three months.

starter.peanut_noodles.title: Peanut noodles with crunchy vegetables
steps: Cook the noodles as the package says, adding the edamame for the last 2 minutes. Drain and rinse under cold water.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, sesame oil and honey with a splash of hot water until smooth and pourable.
Toss the noodles and edamame with the sauce, carrot, cucumber and scallions.
Top with cilantro, and red pepper flakes for anyone who likes heat.
starter.peanut_noodles.notes: Good cold, so it packs well for the next day's lunch.

starter.garlic_shrimp_linguine.title: Garlic and lemon shrimp linguine
steps: Cook the linguine in a large pan of salted boiling water until just tender. Save a mugful of the cooking water, then drain.
Meanwhile, warm the oil and butter in a large frying pan over medium heat and cook the garlic and red pepper flakes for a minute, without letting the garlic brown.
Add the shrimp and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, turning once, until pink and opaque all the way through.
Toss in the linguine, lemon zest and juice, parsley and a splash of the cooking water. Season with salt.

starter.homemade_fish_sticks.title: Homemade fish sticks
steps: Heat the oven to {oven:220} and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Cut the fish into finger-sized strips. Mix the breadcrumbs with the lemon zest.
Dip each strip in the flour, then the egg, then the breadcrumbs, pressing them on. Lay them on the baking sheet and drizzle with the oil.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, turning once, until the coating is golden, crisp and cooked through and the fish is opaque all the way through and flakes easily.
Cool a little, and check for bones before serving to babies.
starter.homemade_fish_sticks.notes: Freeze uncooked fish sticks on a tray, then bag them, for up to two months. Bake from frozen for a few minutes longer.
